full_text_en:
Jiangsu SUNTIME Ship Co., Ltd. Bankruptcy Reorganization Case

Ruling Summary

The bankruptcy reorganization case of Jiangsu SUNTIME Ship Co., Ltd. is a case where the bankruptcy reorganization of a listed company and a major asset reorganization were implemented simultaneously, and the consultation mechanism between the Supreme People's Court and the China Securities Regulatory Commission was initiated in bankruptcy judicial practice. The reorganization procedure and the major asset reorganization procedure were carried out in parallel, which internally required resolving the issue of corporate governance structure under reorganization, and externally required coordinating the conflict between judicial procedures and administrative procedures. Through the consultation mechanism, opinions of the Merger and Acquisition and Reorganization Expert Advisory Committee were formed, and the court, having referred to such opinions, ruled to approve the reorganization plan.

Applicant: Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nantong Chongchuan Sub-branch, domiciled at Yuelong Road, Nantong, Jiangsu Province.
Person in charge: Gu Pengfei, President of the sub-branch.

Respondent: Jiangsu SUNTIME Ship Co., Ltd., domiciled at Software Avenue, Yuhuatai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal representative: Zhang Shunfu, General Manager of the company.

On December 22, 2015, Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nantong Chongchuan Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) applied to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Nanjing Intermediate Court) for reorganization of the respondent, Jiangsu SUNTIME Ship Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as SUNTIME Ship), on the grounds that SUNTIME Ship was unable to pay off its debts as they fell due and its assets were insufficient to cover all its debts. The Nanjing Intermediate Court held a hearing to review the reorganization application in accordance with law.

The Nanjing Intermediate Court found upon investigation that SUNTIME Ship was established in June 2003. Its business scope mainly included ship and non-ship trading, etc. The actual controller was Jiangsu Guoxin Asset Management Group Co., Ltd. In August 2011, the stock of SUNTIME Ship was listed and traded on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. In recent years, due to the persistent downturn in the shipping and ship market and poor management, SUNTIME Ship suffered huge losses since 2014. In 2015, the company's stock was subject to special treatment for "delisting risk warning." The company's operations continued to deteriorate, with liabilities of over RMB 8 billion.

The Nanjing Intermediate Court held that SUNTIME Ship was unable to pay off its debts as they fell due and its existing assets were insufficient to cover all its debts, thus the conditions for reorganization had arisen. On February 5, 2016, the Nanjing Intermediate Court, after reporting level by level to the Supreme People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the SPC) for approval, ruled in accordance with law to accept the bankruptcy reorganization case of SUNTIME Ship.

As SUNTIME Ship had low asset efficiency, heavy debts, and urgent rescue time, the previous model of implementing a major asset reorganization after the reorganization of a listed company could no longer meet the needs of SUNTIME Ship for revival. In view of this, this case adopted a rescue model of simultaneous implementation of reorganization and major asset reorganization. On April 28, 2016, with the authorization of the administrator, SUNTIME Ship held a board meeting, which considered and approved the proposal on major asset reorganization. Thereafter, the administrator formulated a discussion draft for consultation on the draft reorganization plan of SUNTIME Ship, and incorporated the major asset reorganization plan as the main content of the business plan in the draft reorganization plan. The main contents of the draft reorganization plan included: stripping off the original assets, injecting high-quality assets, protecting operational creditors from losses in the reorganization process, and using the company's capital reserve to increase share capital to pay off the remaining unsecured ordinary claims that could not be settled in cash, etc.

In accordance with Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Summary of the Symposium on the Work of Hearing Cases of Bankruptcy Reorganization of Listed Companies (hereinafter referred to as the Symposium Summary), where the draft reorganization plan involves matters subject to administrative licensing by the securities regulatory authority, the court accepting the case shall initiate a consultation mechanism with the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) through the SPC. That is, the SPC sends relevant materials by letter to the CSRC, and the CSRC arranges for the Merger and Acquisition and Reorganization Expert Advisory Committee to study the consultation case. The M&A Expert Advisory Committee shall, in accordance with the same review standards as those of the M&A Review Committee, study the administrative licensing matters submitted for consultation and issue expert advisory opinions. The people's court shall refer to the expert advisory opinions when making a ruling on whether to approve the draft reorganization plan. On July 15, 2016, the Nanjing Intermediate Court initiated the consultation mechanism.

On September 7, 2016, the administrator submitted the draft reorganization plan to the Nanjing Intermediate Court. On September 23, SUNTIME Ship held the second creditors' meeting. The creditors' meeting reviewed and voted on the draft reorganization plan of SUNTIME Ship. The secured creditors' group, tax creditors' group, and ordinary creditors' group all voted to approve the draft reorganization plan. On the same day, SUNTIME Ship held a meeting of the contributors' group and an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders. The meeting reviewed and voted to approve the plan for adjusting the rights and interests of contributors involved in the reorganization plan and all relevant proposals on major asset reorganization. On September 26, the administrator applied to the Nanjing Intermediate Court for a ruling to approve the draft reorganization plan.

The Nanjing Intermediate Court held that, in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law), the draft reorganization plan is to be voted on by the creditors' meeting in groups; where matters involving adjustment of contributors' rights and interests are concerned, a contributors' group should also be established to vote on such matters. After each voting group has voted to approve the draft reorganization plan, it should be submitted to the court for review, and the court shall rule on approval. That is, the procedure for approving the draft reorganization plan is "meeting voting + judicial ruling."

In accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Measures for Major Asset Reorganization, a listed company conducting a major asset reorganization shall have the board of directors make a resolution in accordance with law and submit it to the shareholders' meeting for approval. The CSRC shall, in accordance with statutory conditions and procedures, decide whether to approve the application for major asset reorganization of the listed company. That is, the procedure for major asset reorganization is "internal resolution + administrative licensing."

When a major asset reorganization is initiated simultaneously in the reorganization procedure, there exist conflicts in internal corporate governance structure between "meeting voting" and "internal resolution," as well as conflicts in external regulatory power between "judicial ruling" and "administrative licensing."

I. On the Harmonization of the Governance Structure of the Listed Company and the Administrator Management Model

According to the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the management models of an enterprise during reorganization are divided into the administrator management model and the debtor management model. The difference between the two models lies in the attribution of the enterprise's operational control, which is exercised by the administrator and the debtor respectively, and each is correspondingly responsible for preparing the draft reorganization plan. The Enterprise Bankruptcy Law stipulates that during the reorganization period of an enterprise, the administrator management model is the principle. In practice, the vast majority of listed company reorganizations also adopt this model. Because the parallel operation of reorganization and major asset reorganization procedures is complex, the SUNTIME Ship reorganization case adopted the administrator management model, with the administrator responsible for preparing the draft reorganization plan.

After taking over the company's property and business affairs, the administrator becomes an organ of internal corporate governance, responsible for carrying out the company's reorganization work. However, when the Company Law and Securities Law of our country stipulate resolutions concerning major asset reorganizations of listed companies, they assume that the enterprise is in a normal state of existence, and fail to make exceptional provisions for the state of bankruptcy. In practice, the securities regulatory authority, in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Measures, requires a listed company to have the board of directors make a resolution in accordance with law and submit it to the shareholders' meeting for approval, even when conducting a major asset reorganization during the reorganization procedure. Therefore, if the aforementioned original decision-making organs of the listed company were to be abolished, it would also affect the initiation of a major asset reorganization in the reorganization procedure.

To this end, in this case, under the administrator-responsible model, the administrator was responsible for coordinating and handling many legal matters such as reviewing claims, investigating assets, advancing derivative litigation, disclosing information, and preparing the draft reorganization plan. At the same time, taking into account the necessity of retaining the company's original decision-making organs, the administrator engaged the original management to continue being responsible for the company's daily operations, authorized the board of directors to consider and approve the major asset reorganization proposal, and submitted it to the contributors' group meeting and extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for voting.

II. On the Operation of the Consultation Mechanism between the SPC and the CSRC

To resolve the coordination issues between judicial power and administrative power in the parallel process of reorganization and major asset reorganization, the Symposium Summary established a consultation mechanism between the SPC and the CSRC.

Because consultation takes time, in order to ensure the smooth progress of the reorganization procedure within the prescribed period, this case initiated the consultation mechanism two months before the draft reorganization plan was submitted to the court.

According to the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the court shall convene a creditors' meeting within 30 days from the date of receipt of the draft reorganization plan to vote on it. The administrator or debtor shall, within 10 days from the date the draft is approved, submit an application for approval to the court. The court shall rule on whether to approve within 30 days from the date of receipt of the application. That is, the maximum period from the date the court receives the draft reorganization plan to the date of the ruling on approval is 70 days.

Therefore, if the consultation mechanism were to be initiated at the time of or after the submission of the draft reorganization plan to the court, it would be difficult to meet the consultation needs within the time frame.

According to the Symposium Summary, the court shall refer to the expert advisory opinions when making a ruling on whether to approve the draft reorganization plan. To avoid the situation where, after the draft reorganization plan is approved by voting, the expert advisory opinions hold that the major asset reorganization plan needs to be modified or rejected, causing delays or even failure to obtain approval in the reorganization procedure, this case sent the consultation materials to the CSRC through the SPC as early as before the draft reorganization plan was submitted to the court, hoping to receive the expert advisory opinions before the draft reorganization plan was voted on.

Having the expert advisory opinions issued earlier facilitated timely modification and adjustment of the draft reorganization plan before its formulation and voting. Even if the draft reorganization plan failed to be approved by voting, since the expert advisory opinions serve only as a reference and cannot replace administrative licensing decisions, this would not result in the consequence of unexecuted administrative licensing matters. However, because the timing for the issuance of the consultation opinion was uncertain, and to avoid affecting the reorganization process, the administrator submitted the draft reorganization plan to the Nanjing Intermediate Court in accordance with law. After the draft reorganization plan was approved by voting, on October 22, 2016, the Nanjing Intermediate Court received the expert advisory opinion issued by the CSRC's M&A Expert Advisory Committee.

Upon reviewing the draft reorganization plan and referring to the expert advisory opinion, the Nanjing Intermediate Court considered that the formulation and voting procedures of the reorganization plan were lawful, its content complied with legal provisions, treated creditors fairly, made fair and just adjustments to contributors' rights and interests, and the business plan was feasible. On October 24 of the same year, the Nanjing Intermediate Court, in accordance with Article 86, Paragraph 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Summary of the Symposium on the Work of Hearing Cases of Bankruptcy Reorganization of Listed Companies, ruled: (1) Approving the reorganization plan of SUNTIME Ship; (2) Terminating the reorganization procedure of SUNTIME Ship.
